title: In Psalms 44 How Can We Reconcile The Experience Of Gods Past Faithfulness With Our Current Struggles
paragraphs: Reconciling God’s Past Faithfulness with Present Struggles: A Study of Psalm 44

Psalm 44 presents a profound tension familiar to many believers: How do we reconcile a history of God’s faithfulness with moments in our lives when He seems absent or silent? This psalm, attributed to the sons of Korah, offers a raw and honest prayer that moves from praise to lament, and ultimately, to a plea for God’s intervention.
Remembering God’s Faithfulness (Psalm 44:1–8)
The psalm opens with a collective remembrance of God’s mighty acts on behalf of Israel:
We have heard with our ears, O God, Our fathers have told us, What work thou didst in their days, In the days of old. - Psalm 44:1 ASV

The psalmist recounts stories of God delivering Israel, driving out nations, and planting His people in the land (Psalm 44:2 ASV). The emphasis is clear: the victories were not achieved by the people’s own strength, but by God’s power and favor.

For they gat not the land in possession by their own sword, Neither did their own arm save them; But thy right hand, and thine arm, and the light of thy countenance, Because thou wast favorable unto them. - Psalm 44:3 ASV
This remembrance is an act of worship and trust. The psalmist confesses ongoing reliance on God:
Through thee will we push down our adversaries: Through thy name will we tread them under that rise up against us. - Psalm 44:5 ASV
Present Suffering and Confusion (Psalm 44:9–22)
However, the tone shifts dramatically. Despite this history, Israel is now experiencing defeat, disgrace, and suffering. The psalmist does not shy away from expressing confusion and even pain:
But now thou hast cast us off, and brought us to dishonor, And goest not forth with our hosts. - Psalm 44:9 ASV
What is especially striking is the insistence that this suffering is not due to unfaithfulness or idolatry:
All this is come upon us; yet have we not forgotten thee, Neither have we dealt falsely in thy covenant. - Psalm 44:17 ASV
This raises an important theological tension: Why do God’s faithful people sometimes suffer, even when they are walking in obedience?
Reconciling the Tension: Faith Amid Mystery

Psalm 44 teaches that faith is not based on current circumstances alone, but on the unchanging character and past acts of God. The psalmist’s lament does not result in rejection of God, but leads to earnest prayer:
Awake, why sleepest thou, O Lord? Arise, cast us not off for ever. - Psalm 44:23 ASV
Rise up for our help, And redeem us for thy lovingkindness’ sake. - Psalm 44:26 ASV

This is a model for believers: we can honestly bring our pain and questions to God, while still clinging to His faithfulness. The Bible repeatedly affirms that suffering is not always a sign of God’s displeasure (John 9:1–3 ASV; Romans 8:35–39 ASV).
The New Testament Perspective: Christ in Our Suffering
The Apostle Paul quotes Psalm 44:22 in Romans 8:36 ASV to affirm that suffering—even for the faithful—is not incompatible with God’s love:
Even as it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; We were accounted as sheep for the slaughter. - Romans 8:36 ASV

Yet, Paul triumphantly concludes that nothing can separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus (Romans 8:38–39 ASV). Our ultimate confidence rests not in changeable circumstances, but in the unchanging work and person of Jesus Christ.
Application: Living by Faith, Not by Sight
Remember God’s faithfulness: Recount His past works in the Bible and your own life.
Be honest in prayer: Bring your pain, confusion, and questions to God.
Cling to Christ: Trust that Jesus is God’s ultimate proof of His love and faithfulness, even when you do not understand your circumstances (John 16:33 ASV).
Await God’s redemption: Like the psalmist, continue to call on God, believing in His lovingkindness.
Conclusion

Psalm 44 invites believers to hold together the memory of God’s faithfulness and the reality of current struggles. It teaches that faith involves both remembrance and honest lament, ultimately grounded in the steadfast love of God revealed in Christ.
